questions.prompt: Back Bay was originally what geographic feature before being filled in over several decades?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Tidal flats. Swamp. They filled it in starting in the 1850s. Every building you see is standing on garbage and gravel.
questions.npcReactionWrong: This whole neighborhood is built on lies. Literally. There was nothing here but marsh and mud.

questions.prompt: The Boston Public Library in Copley Square opened its current building in what year?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: 1895. Though the library itself started in 1854. That building has murals by John Singer Sargent. Free to see. Free to use. Imagine.
questions.npcReactionWrong: 1895. The library in Copley Square—the building, not the institution. First publicly supported municipal library in America.

questions.prompt: What architectural style defines most of Back Bay's brownstone townhouses?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Victorian. French Academic influence. They planned the whole thing at once. That's why the streets go in alphabetical order.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Victorian with French influence. The brownstones here all look similar. That's not an accident.

questions.prompt: Back Bay's cross streets are arranged alphabetically. What is the correct sequence from east to west?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Arlington, Berkeley, Clarendon, Dartmouth... all the way to Hereford. Sully used to sing them to remember.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Arlington, Berkeley, Clarendon, Dartmouth, Exeter, Fairfield, Gloucester, Hereford. Then Massachusetts Ave.

questions.prompt: Trinity Church in Copley Square was designed by what famous architect?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: H.H. Richardson. They named a whole style after him: Richardsonian Romanesque. The man was a genius. Died at 47.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Henry Hobson Richardson. Trinity Church—that's the one reflected in the Hancock Tower. An architectural masterpiece.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the name of the skyscraper that reflects Trinity Church in its glass facade?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: John Hancock Tower. 200 Clarendon Street now, officially. There's a famous photograph—old church reflected in modern glass.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: John Hancock Tower. That reflection is one of the most photographed views in Boston.

alternateQuestions.prompt: The Boston Marathon finishes on what Back Bay street?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Boylston Street. Near Copley Square. Every April, runners from all over the world cross that line.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Boylston Street. The finish line is sacred ground in this city.

alternateQuestions.prompt: How many years did it take to fill in Back Bay?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Thirty to forty years. They didn't build this neighborhood overnight. Trainloads of gravel from Needham. Day after day after day.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: The landfill project took decades. Starting in 1857, running into the 1890s. That's dedication. Or stubbornness.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What major thoroughfare runs through the center of Back Bay with a central mall and promenade?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Commonwealth Avenue. The grand boulevard. Walking path down the middle. Modeled after the Champs-Élysées. We aim high.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Commonwealth Avenue. There's a grand boulevard with a walking path down the middle. That's the one.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the name of the large public greenspace where Back Bay meets Beacon Hill?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: The Public Garden. Swan boats. Flower beds. At the east end of Commonwealth Ave. Don't confuse it with the Common.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Boston Public Garden. That's where the swan boats are. The Common is next door. Different parks.

redemptionChallenge.instructions: Four images of Boston buildings are shown. One has been digitally altered. Identify which building has the architectural error.
redemptionChallenge.npcPassResponse: Good eye. Most people can't spot a forgery, architectural or otherwise. Sully had the eye too. Miss that old crook.
redemptionChallenge.npcFailResponse: You thought that building looked correct? That building? My professional reputation is insulted. Study harder.
